strategy.title: No plan inside a $500 capital ceiling: each kit must be prepaid at $900
strategy.why: The only opening (refurbished maglock kits, 4 signed POs at $1,450, pay on delivery) requires paying PuzzleWorks Surplus $900 per kit before shipment, and buyers pay only on delivery. $900 > the $500 capital ceiling, so not even the first kit can be ordered; no plan reaches any settled cash inside the limit.

alternatives.why: With $900, kits can be bought one at a time: each cycle settles in 9 days, so three kits settle by about day 27 for $4,350 of receipts, above the $4,000 target.

alternatives.title: Ask buyers for a deposit
alternatives.why: Not evidenced: the POs say each pays on delivery; no buyer has agreed to prepay.

facts.value: Sell Refurbished maglock puzzle-controller kits for escape room operators to each buyer.
PuzzleWorks Surplus (written quote: $900 per kit, paid before shipment, ships in 3 days) quoted to do the work.
Four escape room operators signed purchase orders at $1,450 per refurbished maglock controller kit (POs dated 2026-11-20); each pays on delivery.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance and the decisive gap is a true constraint, not missing evidence. The only opening has four written POs at $1,450 (pay on delivery) and a recorded fulfiller, PuzzleWorks Surplus, whose written quote requires $900 per kit paid before shipment (card exposure/peakFunding $900). Even with all evidence in hand, the first kit needs $900 out before any cash returns, above the $500 capital ceiling, so the limit cannot be met: nothing settles inside the limits (Brain's own NOT_VIABLE reading agrees). The resolution is correctly sized: $900 is the minimum, and recycling it works (3 x $1,450 = $4,350 >= $4,000 from the 4 signed POs, three 9-day cycles settling by ~day 27; recycling is in fact faster because a settled $1,450 funds the next kit with $550 left over). The deposit alternative is correctly marked unevidenced (POs say pay on delivery) and correctly sized at >= $400 per kit ($900 - $500).
findings: Minor: the recycle schedule is conservative; after kit 1 settles (~day 9) cash of $1,450 + remaining ceiling allows a second kit, and after kit 2 two kits can be ordered at once, so the target could settle earlier than day 27. This does not change the $900 minimum.
The plan correctly cites no decisiveLinks because the gap is a limit the evidence fully determines (CAPITAL constraint based on card field exposure).

reviews.reasons: The contract now allows $2,000 of capital (exposureCap 200000), which removes the constraint the previous NO_PLAN rested on. EXECUTABLE is right: every link is established from the card. There are four written POs at $1,450 per kit (pay on delivery, dated 2026-11-20), a real purchase price from these buyers. The recorded fulfiller is PuzzleWorks Surplus on a written quote of $900 per kit, prepaid, shipping in 3 days, and it is the plan's delivery performer. Time to usable cash is 9 days. Recomputed: wave 1 prepays 2 x $900 = $1,800 (<= $2,000) on day 0 and collects 2 x $1,450 = $2,900 settled on day 9; that funds wave 2's $1,800 on day 9 (cash $2,900 + $200 headroom), which collects $2,900 on day 18. Total settled $5,800 >= $4,000 by day 18 with 12 days of slack, peak exposure $1,800, net after costs $2,200. Wave 1 alone ($2,900) does not reach the target, so recycling is necessary, and it is valid because wave 2 is paid from settled receipts, not new capital. Alternatives are correctly rejected (all four at once needs $3,600 > $2,000).
findings: Brain's check reports 0% coverage for this candidate, apparently because it does not model recycling settled receipts into the second prepayment; the ledger shows the recycle is inside the cap at every point (min cash $200 on day 0), so this is a modelling gap, not a plan defect.

SETTLED_CASH counts gross receipts ($5,800); if the owner reads the goal as net of the $3,600 paid to the supplier, net is $2,200, below $4,000. The contract metric is SETTLED_CASH, so the plan meets it as written.
No buffer for a late payer: if one wave-1 buyer pays late, wave 2 can still order one kit from $1,450 + $200; the target then needs the remaining receipts by day 30, which the 12-day slack covers.
Card records 1 human hour per kit (~4 h); no hours ceiling.
